text.name: dr_lbl_modeKeys
text.text: X / Z: cycle selected output mode

text.name: dr_lbl_sellingOff
text.text: SELLING IS OFF - every market sells on arrival, whatever these rows are set to

text.name: dr_lbl_overviewPointer
text.text: Full breakdown + supply chains: Overview tab

text.name: dr_adv_reserveBad
text.text: Reserve: type a number of litres

text.name: dr_adv_loopOne
text.text: Cannot activate %s - it would loop the product back here.

text.name: dr_adv_loopMany
text.text: %d destination(s) left blocked - they would loop the product back here.

text.name: dr_inp_pooledCapped
text.text: Pooled storage: %s shared by %d products, %d capped. Anything uncapped may use the whole pool.

text.name: dr_inp_pooled
text.text: Pooled storage: %s shared by %d products. Each may use all of it - set a max to reserve room for the others.

text.name: dr_inp_individual
text.text: Set each product's max, or block it. This building has individual per-product storage.

text.name: dr_inp_noSources
text.text: No building on this farm can supply this product.

text.name: dr_set_scope_tt
text.text: Range: every owned asset reaches farm-wide. Proximity: assets only reach sources within the proximity radius below.

text.name: dr_set_includeHusbandry_tt
text.text: Include animal husbandry -- barns, coops, beehives, plus manure & slurry pits -- in the distribution network. Off removes them entirely: they are neither fed nor is their output (milk / manure / slurry / eggs / wool / honey) distributed or sold.

text.name: dr_set_includeSilosSheds_tt
text.text: Include crop / material silos and pallet storage sheds in the distribution network. Off removes them: silos no longer feed productions, and pallet sheds neither receive nor release pallets. (Manure & slurry pits follow the Animal Husbandry setting.)

text.name: dr_set_includeMarkets_tt
text.text: Include markets and kiosks in the distribution network. Off removes them: farm-owned products are no longer routed to them for selling, and the Markets tab is hidden.

text.name: dr_set_includeMapStorage_tt
text.text: Include map storage buildings you do not own but can still store goods in, such as a railway grain pool. Off by default: these buildings normally charge rent for every litre held, so they are added to the network only if you ask. When on, they appear as storage buildings with every product set to Hold, and move nothing until you set them up.

text.name: dr_set_advancedRouting_tt
text.text: Master switch for Advanced Outputs (source-side blocking / priority / Move To) and Advanced Inputs (input blocking / caps / fill targets). Off hides those buttons and reverts to the default nearest-first, distance-based distribution. WARNING: turning this OFF WIPES all existing advanced settings (every block, priority, Move To, input cap and fill target) -- they reset to default and will NOT come back if you turn it on again; you would have to set them up from scratch.

text.name: dr_set_defaultOutputMode_tt
text.text: The output mode given to a building at the moment you PLACE it. Distribute is the normal behaviour. Hold means a newly placed building keeps everything it makes until you set it otherwise, so nothing leaves a building you have not configured yet. On a building that makes pallets this shows as 'Hold Pallets', or as 'Hold Internal' when Pallet spawning is set to never. This ONLY affects buildings placed from now on: existing buildings are never changed, and changing this setting does not touch anything already built.

text.name: dr_set_defaultInputMode_tt
text.text: Whether a newly PLACED building accepts deliveries. Accept all is the normal behaviour. Block all blocks every input on the new building, so nothing is delivered to it until you allow products in from Advanced Inputs. NOTE: Block all only works while Advanced routing is On, because input blocking is part of Advanced routing and is cleared whenever you switch it off. This ONLY affects buildings placed from now on: existing buildings are never changed.

text.name: dr_set_radius_tt
text.text: How far a consumer reaches for sources in Proximity mode.

text.name: dr_set_bufferHours_tt
text.text: Hours of feedstock topped up at each consumer per cycle.

text.name: dr_set_sellEnabled_tt
text.text: Global switch for all auto-selling (Sell / Distribute+Sell modes).

text.name: dr_set_waterSupplyEnabled_tt
text.text: Automatically supply water to water-input productions and animal pastures (billed by distance to the nearest water source).

text.name: dr_set_distCostEnabled_tt
text.text: Charge a per-hour transport cost for each active distribution (scales with haul distance).

text.name: dr_set_distCostBase_tt
text.text: Base transport cost per hour for a short haul (at or under the cost distance below).

text.name: dr_set_distCostThreshold_tt
text.text: Hauls at or under this distance pay the flat base rate; longer hauls scale up linearly.

text.name: dr_set_seasonalReserveEnabled_tt
text.text: Crops set to Distribute+Sell keep enough feedstock to feed production until the next harvest; only the surplus is sold.

text.name: dr_set_seasonalFallbackMonths_tt
text.text: Months of feedstock to hold for a crop before the mod has observed its real harvest window.

text.name: dr_set_bestPriceEnabled_tt
text.text: Master switch: hold Sell / Distribute+Sell surplus until its best month before selling. Off: everything sells immediately.

text.name: dr_set_bestPriceDefault_tt
text.text: Default for any Sell / Distribute+Sell output and for every market product, until you set that building's own toggle. Markets you have already configured keep their setting.

text.name: dr_set_palletSpawnMode_tt
text.text: Whole pallets: pens hold product internally and release a FULL pallet, like productions. Vanilla: a pallet appears at once and fills gradually. Never: nothing spawns pallets on its own, product stays internal and still distributes, stores and sells from there. You can always release one by hand with Spawn Pallets. Never applies to your pens and productions only - beehives keep spawning as normal (they have no internal buffer to sell from), and shops you buy pallets from are never affected.

text.name: dr_set_passThroughStores_tt
text.text: Some mods add a storage building with a fake production attached, where every line turns a product straight back into itself. The production does nothing; it is only there so the game will deliver to the building. Treat as storage makes Distribution Redux see it as the silo it really is, so it stops asking for every litre on the farm and its real lines (if it has any) still show on Productions. The third option also switches those fake lines off in the game itself - tidier, but it is written into your savegame and stays off if you remove this mod.

text.name: dr_set_passThroughStores_v3
text.text: Treat as storage + switch lines off

text.name: dr_set_menuRefresh_tt
text.text: How often the open menu re-reads the farm. The Overview re-enumerates every building and product, so on a large farm a slower rate keeps the menu responsive. Manual only stops the background refresh entirely - the figures still update whenever you select something or press Refresh on the Overview.

text.name: dr_set_debugEnabled_tt
text.text: Write detailed distribution activity to log.txt (moves, sales, stores, water top-ups and charges). Turn off for a quieter log.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_1
text.text: Distribution Redux completely replaces the base game's distribution system. No extra placeables are needed. It works with all default buildings, and with building mods that follow the standard GIANTS schema for their building type. This is very complicated mod and it can be easy to inadvertently create issues/blockages. Please review the entire help guide prior to use.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_3
text.text: Backslash key: open the Distribution Redux menu - a full-screen window with a tab for every kind of building, plus this guide and the settings.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_4
text.text: Left-bracket key: while on foot, look at a building's loading or unloading point to open the menu straight to that building's page. The prompt only appears when you are looking at one of your own buildings that is part of the network.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_5
text.text: Both keys can be rebound under Options - Controls.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_7
text.text: Open the menu, pick the building you care about, and set each product to Hold, Distribute, Sell, and so on. That is the whole loop - everything else is detail.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_8
text.text: ## What it does differently to base game

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_9
text.text: - Allows any building that stores, produces, feeds or sells to participate in the distribution.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_10
text.text: - Will deliver only what the demand needs rather than trying to fill to capacity

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_11
text.text: - Charges for distribution based on distance

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_12
text.text: - Allows you to Sell Immediately or wait until best price is reached

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_13
text.text: - Allows a seasonal reserve to be held for seasonal crops to ensure productions can continue, only selling the un-needed portion of the harvest

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_14
text.text: - Auto-watering will pull water from any storage or the nearest water source (e.g. lake) to supply demand

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_15
text.text: - Allows you to override the default distribution mechanism to prioritise demands, Block specific Inputs and Outputs, Set Output Reserves, and Set Input demand targets

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_17
text.text: - Allocate - Build a demand list from every consumer: production inputs, animal food, feeding-robot bunkers, straw, husbandry water. Then match sources to demand nearest-first, honouring per-product blocks, priorities and input caps.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_18
text.text: - Move the remainder - Store leftovers in available storage buildings, Move Stock to available markets, then Move stock between storages, honouring per-product blocks, priorities and input caps.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_19
text.text: - Charge - Distance-based haulage billing, plus the vanilla per-hour production running costs (which are otherwise lost because DR suppresses the base hourly pass).

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_20
text.text: - Sell / Market Supply - Sell surplus, sell out of market buffers, then sell direct outputs (e.g. electricity, methane), honouring any seasonal harvest, and sell immediate vs sell at best price rules.

text.name: dr_guide_gettingStarted_21
text.text: - Account - Record Production and husbandry throughput, calculate manual load/unload deltas, emit the money summary.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_1
text.text: The backslash key opens the consolidated menu. Down the left side are tabs.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_4
text.text: - Silos - bulk silos and pallet / bale storage sheds, plus manure and slurry pits.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_5
text.text: - Animal Husbandry - barns, coops, pens and beehives.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_6
text.text: - Markets - the kiosks and markets you have placed on the map.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_7
text.text: - Overview - detailed figures for every building and every product in one table.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_10
text.text: Each building tab is a two-pane page: your buildings listed on the left, and the selected building's incoming products, production lines and outgoing products on the right. Exactly which of those three lists appear depends on what the building does.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_12
text.text: Every building tab, and the Overview tab, has a Timescale selector at the top offering Hour, Month and Year. It rescopes the flow figures on that page - what was received, consumed, produced, distributed and sold in that window.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_13
text.text: A Distribution Redux "month" is 24 hourly passes, so Month means roughly the last in-game day regardless of how many real days you have set per period. Held is never rescoped: it is a stock, not a flow, so it always shows what is in the building right now.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_14
text.text: Year data builds up over time. There was no year-scale record before this feature existed, so on an older save the Year column starts empty and fills as each in-game month completes.

text.name: dr_guide_theMenu_16
text.text: The Silos, Animal Husbandry and Markets tabs only appear when that group is switched on in Settings. Switch a group off and its buildings leave the distribution network entirely and its tab disappears. Turn the group back on to get both back.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_1
text.text: The Productions, Silos, Markets and Animal Husbandry tabs share one layout: pick a building on the left, then configure its products on the right. Tables and Column sets differ slightly by building type, because not every building consumes or produces.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_5
text.text: - HELD/MAX - how much of it is in the building now, the Max amount that could be stored and the max set amount in Brackets as a percentage.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_6
text.text: - FREE STORAGE - How much more of this product the building can hold, taking into account the max set amount (%) and remaining space.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_7
text.text: - RECIEVED - how much of the product Distribution Redux delivered to this building in the selected timescale.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_8
text.text: - CONSUMED - how much of the product the building used in the selected timescale. Productions and Animal Husbandry only.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_9
text.text: - STATUS - Active (Recieving) or Active (Idle), based on activity in the last cycle, or Blocked.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_11
text.text: - PRODUCTION LINES - the product the line makes, with its inputs in brackets.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_12
text.text: - STATUS - Running, Idle (switched on but missing inputs), or Off.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_13
text.text: - TARGET /mo - how much that line is expected to produce per month if all inputs are provided.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_16
text.text: - HELD (MAX) - how much of this product is in the building now, with capacity in brackets.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_17
text.text: - FREE STORAGE - How much more of this product the building can hold

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_18
text.text: - PRODUCED - how much was produced in the selected timescale. Productions and Animal Husbandry only.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_19
text.text: - DISTRIBUTED - everything that left: distributed, stored, moved and sold combined, with the sale value in brackets when any of it sold.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_20
text.text: - OUTPUT MODE - the mode this output is currently set to.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_21
text.text: - STATUS - Active (Sending) or Active (Idle), based on activity in the last cycle, or Blocked.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_23
text.text: - If a building can have both internal storage and pallets, the display will show the internal amount and then the amount stored in Pallets on the buildings pallet spawner

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_24
text.text: - The Selected timeframe will only show material that has been moved in that timeframe, if you have only just activated the production and are showing Annual, you will only see what's moved since you activated it.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_25
text.text: - More details on what is going where is available on the overview tab

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_26
text.text: - Volumes switch unit at 1,000 litres. Up to 999 L they read in litres; from 1,000 L up they read in kilolitres with any extraneous zeros dropped, so 1,001 L shows as 1.001 kL, 123,123 L as 123.123 kL, and 600,000 L simply as 600 kL. Three decimals is exactly one litre, so nothing is lost in the change of unit.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_27
text.text: - To see if a change has taken effect (ie idle or running), you will need to go through one cycle (1 hour) before the UI column refreshes. If you have a chain of distributions, you may have to cycle through a number of hours until all steps refresh.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_29
text.text: - To turn a production line on or off, select the line and press Toggle Line.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_30
text.text: - To change what happens to an output, select it and press Cycle Output.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_31
text.text: - Advanced opens the per-product routing controls (see Advanced Inputs and Outputs).

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_32
text.text: - Sell Timing appears for an output in a selling mode.

text.name: dr_guide_buildingPages_33
text.text: Changing a production output or toggling a production line here is the same setting as the vanilla production screen's output toggle, so either place updates the other - and the vanilla screen shows the mod's mode names too.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_1
text.text: ## Which modes each building type offers

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_2
text.text: - Productions - Distribute, Store, Hold Pallets, Hold Internal, Sell, Market Supply.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_3
text.text: - Silos and storage - Distribute, Move To, Hold, Sell, Market Supply.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_4
text.text: - Animal Husbandry - Distribute, Store, Hold Pallets, Hold Internal, Sell, Market Supply.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_6
text.text: Not every mode is offered all the time. If a mode has no possible end point it is hidden rather than shown as a dead end. E.g. with no market placed, or no market that accepts the product, Market Supply does not appear in the list.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_8
text.text: - Distribute - feed nearby productions and animals that need this product, nearest source first, up to what their recipes call for. Surplus stays put.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_9
text.text: - Store - move the output into any storage building that accepts it, nearest first, spilling to the next when one fills. Productions and Animal Husbandry.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_10
text.text: - Move To - move product from one storage building to another that accepts it. Storage buildings only. See the warning below.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_11
text.text: - Hold Internal - keep the output as bulk inside the building; no pallets spawn on their own and you spawn them yourself on demand (see Pallet Spawning).

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_12
text.text: - Hold Pallets - keep the output where it is, as pallets, and let it accumulate.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_13
text.text: - Sell - sell the product, either immediately or at the best price (see Sell Timing).

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_14
text.text: - Market Supply - transfer the output to a market or kiosk you have placed, where it sells at a premium.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_16
text.text: - Distribute + Sell - feed all demand first, then sell what is left.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_17
text.text: - Distribute + Store - feed demand first, then move the surplus into your storage instead of selling it. Productions and Animal Husbandry only.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_18
text.text: - Distribute + Move To - feed demand first, then move the surplus to your chosen storage. Storage buildings only.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_19
text.text: - Distribute + Market Supply - feed demand first, then transfer the surplus to your market or kiosk.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_20
text.text: In every combined mode the first half genuinely happens first. Nothing is sold, stored or shipped to a market until consumers have been offered it.

text.name: dr_guide_outputModes_21
text.text: Move To is only offered if advanced routing is activated (See Advanced Routing).

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_2
text.text: Advanced routing lets you control every individual input and output of every building. It is switched on by default and can be turned off in Settings.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_4
text.text: - Select any incoming product and press Advanced Inputs.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_5
text.text: - Block / Allow - stop this building from ever receiving that product.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_6
text.text: - Block All / Allow All - flip every input at once.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_7
text.text: - Max In - the most of that product the building may hold. This matters for pooled storage, where several products share one tank. A pool is first come, first served: by default every product may use all of it, exactly as the base game behaves. That means a busy product can fill a silo and leave little room for the others - so set Max In on that product to cap it and hold space back for the rest. Caps are independent and do not have to add up to 100 percent; anything you leave alone stays unlimited.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_8
text.text: - Target - a fill target for that product. Instead of delivering only what the next cycle needs, the network works towards this level and then holds it - in effect an input reserve.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_10
text.text: - Select the outgoing product you want to adjust and press Advanced Outputs.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_11
text.text: - Block / Allow - never send this output to that destination.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_12
text.text: - Prioritise - rank the demands and storage options for this output. This overrides the default nearest-first-then-spill behaviour.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_13
text.text: - Reserve (+/-) - keep this many litres in the building at all times. Nothing - distributing, selling, storing, moving or market supply - may take the product below this figure.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_15
text.text: - This mode is only available as an output mode when Advanced Routing is turned on and the building is type: Storage

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_16
text.text: - This mode allows you to move the materials in that storage to another storage that supports it

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_17
text.text: - By default when you activate this every possible destination is blocked to avoid accidental creation of product loops

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_18
text.text: - To Active this, select any output, and press Advanced Outputs. You will see a list of supporting destinations on the right (All Blocked) and you can allow buildings as needed. All other advanced output functions are also available for this Move (Prioritise, Reserve etc).

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_19
text.text: - By Default move to will try to fill the building as much as possible in each cycle. You can set a "Max In" on the receiving buildings inputs to ensure you have space to move multiple products (rather than just completely filling the silo with the first product).

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_21
text.text: - Every advanced setting you have made is erased, not merely ignored - all blocks, priorities, reserves, Max In values and targets. Turning Advanced routing back on later gives you a clean slate, so you will need to set it all up again.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_23
text.text: These advanced rules apply whether or not Advanced Routing is on, seasonal harvest reserve and AutWater can be turned on/off in settings if desired.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_25
text.text: For any output in a selling mode you can choose to sell immediately or to wait for the best price. Waiting means the product accumulates in the building until the peak arrives, so make sure there is room for it.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_27
text.text: Switched OFF by default. When you turn it on, an output that is an annual harvest crop will keep roughly a year's worth back to feed your own productions and sell only the surplus. Grass and other crops that regrow through the year keep three months instead. Until the mod has seen a crop harvested it does not know when the next harvest is due, so it falls back to the Reserve months setting.

text.name: dr_guide_advancedRoutingRules_29
text.text: Water is supplied automatically to any building that needs it, from the nearest water source, while Auto-Water is on. If there is no placed water source, the system will source it from the nearest body of water (note that if the nearest body of water is distant the distribution cost will be high)

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_1
text.text: The Overview tab puts the entire network in one table: every enrolled building, and every product going into or out of it. It is the place to look when you want to know what is actually happening rather than what a single building is set to.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_2
text.text: Each product is tagged (In), (Out) or (In/Out) so you can see at a glance which side of the building it sits on. Silos and sheds are In/Out for everything, since they both receive and supply.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_4
text.text: - Filter by - Nothing (show all), Building, Product, or End product (full chain).

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_5
text.text: - Show - picks which building or product the filter applies to.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_6
text.text: - Timescale - Hour, Month or Year, as on the building tabs.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_7
text.text: - Grouping - Off shows one row per building; On combines buildings of the same type into a single summed row, labelled for example "Bakery x2".

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_8
text.text: End product (full chain) is the most useful of these. Pick a finished product such as cake and the table shows every building and every intermediate product that feeds it, ordered from the finished item back down the chain. It is the quickest way to find the bottleneck or the oversupply in a production line.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_10
text.text: - RECEIVED - delivered to this building by Distribution Redux.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_11
text.text: - LOADED - put into this building by anything that is NOT Distribution Redux: you with a trailer, a bale, an AI helper, another mod.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_12
text.text: - CONSUMED (EXP.) - used up, with the expected figure in brackets.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_13
text.text: - UNLOADED - taken out of this building by anything that is not Distribution Redux, including a pallet you drive away.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_14
text.text: - HELD (CAP) - what is in the building right now, with capacity. Never rescoped by Timescale.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_15
text.text: - PRODUCED (EXP.) - made by this building, with the expected figure in brackets.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_17
text.text: - STORED/MOVED - sent to storage, or moved to another store.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_18
text.text: - SOLD - sold, whether directly or through a market.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_19
text.text: - DISTR. COST - what the haulage for this building's deliveries cost. Charged to the sending building only, so the column adds up to the money actually spent rather than counting each delivery twice.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_20
text.text: ## The expected figures and their colours

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_21
text.text: CONSUMED and PRODUCED carry the expected amount in brackets, worked out from the recipes of the production lines that are switched on. The figure is coloured green when it is at or very near target, orange when it is slightly short, and red when it is well short. Only productions have a recipe, so animal husbandry and silo rows show a plain figure with no target rather than an invented one.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_22
text.text: A red PRODUCED figure is the fastest way to spot a starved line.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_24
text.text: At the bottom of the page you have a button to switch between Show Flows and Show Settings. If you have a production line blocked you can quickly switch to the Show Settings page to see what setting might be blocking it.

text.name: dr_guide_overviewTab_25
text.text: Double-Clicking on a line in either view will take you directly to that buildings page.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_1
text.text: Many outputs are delivered on pallets - boards, planks, vegetables in crates, eggs, wool and so on. To ensure Distribution Redux operates as expected, how pallets work has been completely rewritten

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_2
text.text: Distribution Redux will take into account both product held internally in the building as well as any pallet that is on the buildings pallet spawner for both informational displays AND Output Modes. Distribution will always pull from the pallet spawner first and then the internal Storage. If the pallet spawner is blocked product will accumulate in the buildings own internal storage and distribute from there. A pallet removed from the spawner manually is immediately removed from the buildings total.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_3
text.text: Buildings without a proper pallet pad in their model - some modded spawners, and a few beehives - fall back to a simple nearest-building rule instead.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_5
text.text: - Set the output to Hold Internal. Once it holds at least one full pallet's worth, a Spawn Pallets button appears, both on the Productions tab and on the base-game production screen. Press it to open the spawn window.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_6
text.text: - Type - the pallet type. If the output supports only one it is shown for reference; if it supports several, use the arrows to choose.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_7
text.text: - Quantity - how many to spawn. The arrows step by one, the -10 / +10 buttons jump in tens, and the total is capped by the stock you hold.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_8
text.text: - Spawn drops that many filled pallets at the building's pallet point and removes the matching stock. Cancel closes without spawning.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_9
text.text: The button only appears for an output on Hold Internal holding at least one full pallet's worth - below that there is nothing to spawn. The building must also have a pallet spawn point in its model, which most palletising buildings do. In multiplayer the host performs the spawn, so the pallets appear for everybody.

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_11
text.text: In the default game animal pens spawn a pallet and load it with what is in the internal storage every hour regardless of whether there is enough for a full pallet or not (unlike productions). To keep everything consistent by default animal husbandries have been changed to operate the same as productions. This can be changed in the settings to revert back to base game mode, but this may impact on distribution and distribution tracking data (Not Recommended)

text.name: dr_guide_palletManagement_12
text.text: There is also an option in the same setting to never spawn pallets. This will prevent pallets from ever spawning and just utilise the buildings internal storage to distribute.

text.name: dr_guide_otherChangesToBaseGameMechanics_title
text.text: Other Changes to Base Game Mechanics

text.name: dr_guide_otherChangesToBaseGameMechanics_2
text.text: - When opening a bunker silo, you now only need to hit R and the mod will remove the entire cover off the silo (no more partial covers that can't be removed)

text.name: dr_guide_otherChangesToBaseGameMechanics_3
text.text: - Bunker Silos expect you to create the output by loading material in, covering it, waiting for it to ferment, then uncovering it. As such Distribution Redux only shows the output table and options, and will only show stock once the material is uncovered.

text.name: dr_guide_otherChangesToBaseGameMechanics_5
text.text: - Manure Heaps and slurry pits can now be placed anywhere on the map, and DO NOT auto-attach to an animal husbandry. To move material from an animal husbandry to these objects, place it, and on the barn select "Store" as the output mode. Manure and slurry will move to those buildings just like any other output.

text.name: dr_guide_otherChangesToBaseGameMechanics_7
text.text: - Silo Extensions have been extensively rewritten and now operate differently to base game. Silo Extension can now only be placed within 50m of an existing silo, heap or pit and ONLY add storage space to that buidling.

text.name: dr_guide_otherChangesToBaseGameMechanics_9
text.text: - You can still manually tip/drop off products at your own markets/stalls. Rather than just sell immediately as in base game these products will respect the output mode set on the market.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_1
text.text: Global settings live on the Settings tab. They are saved with your SaveGame and synced in multiplayer by the host. Per-building choices always override these globals for that building.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_3
text.text: - Listed in the order they appear on the tab.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_4
text.text: - Scope - Range (whole farm) or Proximity (within a radius).

text.name: dr_guide_settings_5
text.text: - Animal Husbandry - include or exclude barns, coops, pens and beehives.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_6
text.text: - Silos & Pallet Storage - include or exclude bulk silos, pallet and bale sheds, and manure and slurry pits.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_7
text.text: - Markets & Kiosks - include or exclude your markets and kiosks.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_8
text.text: - Advanced routing - master switch for Advanced Inputs and Advanced Outputs. Off also removes Move To and erases every advanced setting (see Advanced Inputs and Outputs).

text.name: dr_guide_settings_9
text.text: - Proximity radius - how far a source reaches in Proximity scope. Default 50 m.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_10
text.text: - Consumer buffer - hours of feedstock topped up at each consumer per cycle. Default 2.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_11
text.text: - Selling - master on / off for all selling. Off means nothing is ever sold, whatever individual outputs are set to.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_12
text.text: - Auto-Water - automatically supply water to buildings that consume it.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_13
text.text: - Distribution cost - whether haulage is charged at all.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_14
text.text: - Cost rate - the base charge per link per hour. Default 10.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_15
text.text: - Cost distance - the distance increment the rate is multiplied by. Default 50 m.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_16
text.text: - Seasonal harvest reserve - keep enough feedstock to last until the next harvest, selling only the surplus. Off by default.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_17
text.text: - Reserve months (until learned) - how many months to hold back before the mod has learned a crop's harvest window. Default 13.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_18
text.text: - Sell at best price - master on / off for best-price selling. Off means everything sells immediately.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_19
text.text: - Default sell timing - what a new output uses when you have not set it: wait for the peak, or sell immediately.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_20
text.text: - Pallet Spawning - Three options, default game (Spawn partial pallets), Spawn full pallets only (DEFAULT) and Never Spawn Pallets.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_21
text.text: - Menu Refresh Rate - Can be adjusted if you are experiencing lag or stuttering on the UI. Manual will activate a refresh button you can use to refresh the UI.

text.name: dr_guide_settings_22
text.text: - Debug logging - write detailed activity to log.txt. Leave off for a quieter log.

text.name: dr_guide_support_2
text.text: - A building is not showing up. Check Scope and the group toggles. Proximity only reaches within the radius, and a building whose group is switched off is removed from the network and its tab hidden.

text.name: dr_guide_support_3
text.text: - Nothing is being delivered. Make sure the source is set to a Distribute mode rather than Hold, the consumer's production line is switched on, and the two are within reach for the current scope.

text.name: dr_guide_support_4
text.text: - A Move To output is not moving anything. Move To starts with every destination blocked. Open Advanced Outputs and activate the destination you want. If a destination shows "Active - Invalid" in red, activating it would create a loop.

text.name: dr_guide_support_5
text.text: - Something arrived but did not sell this hour. That is intended. Product that has just arrived waits one pass so consumers get first refusal.

text.name: dr_guide_support_6
text.text: - An animal pen is holding its eggs or wool. With "Whole pallets from pens" on, a pen accumulates until it has a full pallet before releasing one. Consumers can still draw on the stock while it fills; selling and storing wait for the pallet.

text.name: dr_guide_support_7
text.text: - A factory is not getting water. Water is supplied automatically while Auto-Water is on; if a water-input plant looks starved, confirm the setting.

text.name: dr_guide_support_8
text.text: - No prompt at a building. The left-bracket prompt only shows for buildings that are part of the network. If you excluded that group in Settings, the prompt is gone by design.

text.name: dr_guide_support_9
text.text: - The mod is not behaving as expected. Do not run this alongside other distribution-overhaul mods - they hook the same system and will fight. The mod works with base-game buildings and with modded buildings that follow the standard GIANTS schema; some modded buildings may behave differently and may impact this mod.

text.name: dr_guide_support_11
text.text: Overviews and guides are on my YouTube channel, @AussieSimmer.

text.name: dr_guide_support_13
text.text: Bugs, feature requests and mod compatibility requests can be raised as a ticket on my GitHub repository:

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_2
text.text: 1. Numerous Bug Fixes (see GitHub for full details).

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_3
text.text: 2. Numerous QoL Additions (see GitHub for full details).

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_4
text.text: 3. Compatibility added for many mods, and the code strengthened to improve mod compatibility overall (see GitHub for full details).

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_5
text.text: 4. Added an Overview tab that allows you to see all distribution activity, and distribution settings, for all buildings in one place (includes filters, and can be set to show all sources and productions contributing to a specific end product)

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_6
text.text: 5. Added Advanced Input and Output management (block, prioritise, reserve stock, fill target, max in).

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_7
text.text: 6. Added the ability to move and sort product between storages (i.e. Silos, Pallet Stores etc)

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_9
text.text: 1. Renaming buildings - every building in the distribution network can now be given a custom name from the base-game construction menu. The game only allows this on some buildings by default; Distribution Redux enables it for all of its buildings (silos, sheds, pits and markets included). The mod then uses your name everywhere in this menu, with the original building name shown underneath it as a reference, so a farm with eight identical greenhouses is finally readable.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_10
text.text: 2. Manure Heap / Slurry Pit product fix - each was listing the other's product as an output. The Manure Heap now shows only Manure, and the Slurry Pit only Slurry.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_11
text.text: 3. Manure Heap / Slurry Pit incoming fix - neither showed an incoming product. They now list what actually flows into them (manure and slurry respectively).

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_13
text.text: 1. UI improvements and a consistency pass, including scroll bars, repositioned tables, and the value of products sold added to the sold column.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_14
text.text: 2. Added Markets and Kiosks to the distribution system - all buildings now have a Market Supply option to route their output to a market you have placed. Items sold through your market get a 20% price bonus, although selling in bulk reduces the price you get, just like the base game.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_15
text.text: 3. Sell at Best Price fix - with no pricing history the system sold earlier than expected. It now falls back to the in-game price graph until it has gathered enough of its own data.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_16
text.text: 4. Added Hold Internal mode and manual pallet spawning - palletisable outputs can be kept as bulk stock instead of auto-spawning pallets, then spawned by hand through a spawn window where you pick the pallet type and quantity. Available from both the Productions tab and the base-game production screen.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_18
text.text: 1. Added the ability to specify whether goods should sell immediately or once they hit best price.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_19
text.text: 2. Completely rebuilt UI that breaks out distribution types and consolidates the settings and help guide into the menu.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_20
text.text: 3. Fixes to silo extensions so they work in a consistent manner. An extension must now be placed within the vicinity of a matching silo type; all distribution is managed in the primary silo and the extension simply adds storage to it.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_21
text.text: 4. Pallet and bale sheds now display all active pallets in the network so they can be pre-configured before items arrive. Added a reserve function that sells pallets (least valuable first) to keep space free for the next cycle - bypassed if another pallet shed has space, in which case pallets are moved there instead.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_22
text.text: 5. Pallet shed interaction fixed: look at the loading-point icon in-game to open that building's distribution page directly.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_23
text.text: 6. Fixed a small amount of output being left in the source after distribution (a timing issue).

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_24
text.text: 7. Biogas plant fixed: methane and electrical charge sales now take game difficulty into account, and digestate now properly registers as Biogas Plant income on the finance sheet.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_25
text.text: 8. Settings reworked to be more granular: you can now include or exclude silos / pallet sheds, and include or exclude animal husbandry buildings. Productions always register and participate in distribution, just like the base game.

text.name: dr_guide_changelog_26
text.text: 9. Change in mode titles: Hold now holds items in the building (used to be "Stored"); Store moves items offsite when storage is available.

text.text: past peak - value falls with age
